## Motivation

::: {.incremental}
- Pitcher fatigue is one of the **hardest things to quantify** in baseball
- Coaches rely on pitch count and gut feel — but when does performance actually decline?
- TrackMan pitch-tracking data gives us a window into **biomechanical changes pitch-by-pitch**
- Can we detect fatigue **before** it becomes visible to the naked eye?
:::

---

## Research Question

::: {.r-fit-text}
Can biomechanical deviations from a  
pitcher's personal baseline predict  
velocity decline within a game?
:::

---

## Data

- **5 games** from UConn's February series vs. Arizona (2/17 – 2/22)
- TrackMan pitch-tracking data with full biomechanical output

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `RelSpeed` | Release velocity (mph) |
| `SpinRate` | Spin rate (rpm) |
| `InducedVertBreak` | Vertical movement (in) |
| `HorzBreak` | Horizontal movement (in) |
| `Extension` | Release extension (ft) |
| `EffectiveVelo` | Perceived velocity at plate |

---

## Methodology: Personalized Baselines

Rather than league averages, we build a **per-pitcher, per-game, per-pitch-type** baseline

```python
# First 20% of each pitcher's outing = baseline window
data_all["BaselineCutoff"] = np.ceil(data_all["TotalPitches"] * 0.20)
data_all["IsBaseline"]     = data_all["PitchCount"] <= data_all["BaselineCutoff"]
```

::: {.callout-note}
This accounts for natural variation across pitchers and pitch types — 
a 90 mph fastball for one pitcher is not the same as 90 mph for another.
:::

---

## Deviation Features

For each pitch, we compute deviation from that pitcher's baseline:

$$\text{VeloDev} = \text{RelSpeed} - \text{BaselineVelo}$$

We compute this for **8 biomechanical features**:

`VeloDev` · `SpinDev` · `IVBDev` · `EffectiveVeloDev`  
`HorzBreakDev` · `PlateHeightDev` · `PlateSideDev` · `ExtensionDev`

> Negative values = below personal baseline = potential fatigue signal

---

## Setup

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, roc_auc_score, ConfusionMatrixDisplay

df_2_17 = pd.read_csv("/Users/shubhantamhane/proposal-latex-repo-ShubhanTamhane1/data/UConn_v_Arizona_State_2.17.csv")
df_2_19 = pd.read_csv("/Users/shubhantamhane/proposal-latex-repo-ShubhanTamhane1/data/UConn_v_Arizona_2.19.csv")
df_2_20 = pd.read_csv("/Users/shubhantamhane/proposal-latex-repo-ShubhanTamhane1/data/UConn_v_Arizona_2.20.csv")
df_2_21 = pd.read_csv("/Users/shubhantamhane/proposal-latex-repo-ShubhanTamhane1/data/UConn_v_Arizona_2.21.csv")
df_2_22 = pd.read_csv("/Users/shubhantamhane/proposal-latex-repo-ShubhanTamhane1/data/UConn_v_Arizona_2.22.csv")

for df, gid in zip([df_2_17,df_2_19,df_2_20,df_2_21,df_2_22],["2_17","2_19","2_20","2_21","2_22"]):
    df["GameID"] = gid

game_order = {"2_17":1,"2_19":2,"2_20":3,"2_21":4,"2_22":5}
data_all = pd.concat([df_2_17,df_2_19,df_2_20,df_2_21,df_2_22], ignore_index=True)
data_all["GameNumber"] = data_all["GameID"].map(game_order)
data_all = data_all.sort_values(["GameNumber","Pitcher","PitchNo"]).copy()
data_all["PitchCount"]     = data_all.groupby(["GameID","Pitcher"])["PitchNo"].rank(method="first")
data_all["TotalPitches"]   = data_all.groupby(["GameID","Pitcher"])["PitchNo"].transform("count")
data_all["BaselineCutoff"] = np.ceil(data_all["TotalPitches"] * 0.20)
data_all["IsBaseline"]     = data_all["PitchCount"] <= data_all["BaselineCutoff"]

def add_baselines(df):
    baseline = (
        df[df["IsBaseline"]]
        .groupby(["GameID","Pitcher","TaggedPitchType"])
        .agg({"RelSpeed":"mean","SpinRate":"mean","InducedVertBreak":"mean",
              "EffectiveVelo":"mean","HorzBreak":"mean","PlateLocHeight":"mean",
              "PlateLocSide":"mean","Extension":"mean"})
        .rename(columns={"RelSpeed":"BaselineVelo","SpinRate":"BaselineSpin",
                         "InducedVertBreak":"BaselineIVB","EffectiveVelo":"BaselineEffectiveVelo",
                         "HorzBreak":"BaselineHorzBreak","PlateLocHeight":"BaselinePlateHeight",
                         "PlateLocSide":"BaselinePlateSide","Extension":"BaselineExtension"})
        .reset_index()
    )
    return df.merge(baseline, on=["GameID","Pitcher","TaggedPitchType"], how="left")

data_all = add_baselines(data_all)
data_all["VeloDev"]          = data_all["RelSpeed"]          - data_all["BaselineVelo"]
data_all["SpinDev"]          = data_all["SpinRate"]          - data_all["BaselineSpin"]
data_all["IVBDev"]           = data_all["InducedVertBreak"]  - data_all["BaselineIVB"]
data_all["EffectiveVeloDev"] = data_all["EffectiveVelo"]     - data_all["BaselineEffectiveVelo"]
data_all["HorzBreakDev"]     = data_all["HorzBreak"]         - data_all["BaselineHorzBreak"]
data_all["PlateHeightDev"]   = data_all["PlateLocHeight"]    - data_all["BaselinePlateHeight"]
data_all["PlateSideDev"]     = data_all["PlateLocSide"]      - data_all["BaselinePlateSide"]
data_all["ExtensionDev"]     = data_all["Extension"]         - data_all["BaselineExtension"]

fastballs = data_all[data_all["TaggedPitchType"] == "Fastball"].copy()
fastballs = fastballs.sort_values(["Pitcher","GameID","PitchCount"]).copy()

def plot_binned_feature(df, feature_col, y_label, title, bins=8):
    plot_df = df.dropna(subset=["PitchCount", feature_col]).copy()
    plot_df["PitchBin"] = pd.cut(plot_df["PitchCount"], bins=bins)
    bin_means = plot_df.groupby("PitchBin", observed=False)[feature_col].mean()
    bin_centers = [interval.mid for interval in bin_means.index]
    plt.figure(figsize=(9,5))
    plt.scatter(plot_df["PitchCount"], plot_df[feature_col], alpha=0.30)
    plt.plot(bin_centers, bin_means.values, linewidth=3)
    plt.axhline(0, color="red")
    plt.xlabel("Pitch Count")
    plt.ylabel(y_label)
    plt.title(title)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

one_pitcher = fastballs[fastballs["Pitcher"] == pitcher_name].copy()
game_id = one_pitcher["GameID"].iloc[0]

## OLS: Is Velocity Decline Statistically Significant?

For each pitcher-game pair:

$$\text{VeloDev}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{PitchCount}_i + \varepsilon_i$$

```{python}
summary = []
for (pitcher, game), df in fastballs.groupby(["Pitcher","GameID"]):
    df = df.dropna(subset=["PitchCount","VeloDev"])
    if len(df) < 10:
        continue
    X = sm.add_constant(df["PitchCount"])
    model = sm.OLS(df["VeloDev"], X).fit()
    cutoff = np.percentile(df["PitchCount"], 80)
    late = df[df["PitchCount"] >= cutoff]
    summary.append({"Pitcher":pitcher, "GameID":game,
                    "Slope":round(model.params["PitchCount"], 4),
                    "p_value":round(model.pvalues["PitchCount"], 4),
                    "Significant (p<0.05)": "✓" if model.pvalues["PitchCount"] < 0.05 else "",
                    "LateGameVeloDev":round(late["VeloDev"].mean(), 3),
                    "NumPitches":len(df)})

summary_df = pd.DataFrame(summary)
summary_df["GameNumber"] = summary_df["GameID"].map(game_order)
summary_df_sorted = summary_df.sort_values("Slope")

display_cols = ["Pitcher","GameID","Slope","p_value","Significant (p<0.05)","LateGameVeloDev","NumPitches"]
summary_df_sorted[display_cols].style.set_properties(**{"font-size":"12px"})
```

## Fatigue Slope Across Games

```{python}
game_summary = (
    summary_df.groupby("GameNumber")
    .agg(AvgSlope=("Slope","mean"), StdSlope=("Slope","std"), Count=("Slope","count"))
    .reset_index()
)

plt.figure(figsize=(9,5))
plt.plot(game_summary["GameNumber"], game_summary["AvgSlope"], marker="o", linewidth=2)
plt.axhline(0, color="red")
plt.xlabel("Game Number")
plt.ylabel("Average Velocity Decline Slope")
plt.title("Average Fatigue Slope Across Games")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## OLS: Fatigue Compounds Across the Series

```{python}
X_game = sm.add_constant(summary_df["GameNumber"])
y_game = summary_df["Slope"]
game_model = sm.OLS(y_game, X_game).fit()
print(game_model.summary())
```

## Approach 1: Outcome-Based Target

**First attempt:** label a pitch as ineffective if it resulted in a ball call

$$y = \mathbf{1}[\text{PitchCall} = \text{"BallCalled"}]$$

**Features:** `VeloDev` · `SpinDev` · `IVBDev` · `EffectiveVeloDev` · `HorzBreakDev` · `ExtensionDev` · `PitchCount`

**Model:** Logistic Regression with `class_weight='balanced'`

---

## Approach 1: Results

```{python}
data_all["Ineffective_outcome"] = (data_all["PitchCall"] == "BallCalled").astype(int)
features_v1 = ["VeloDev","SpinDev","IVBDev","EffectiveVeloDev","HorzBreakDev","ExtensionDev","PitchCount"]
model_df_v1 = data_all.dropna(subset=features_v1 + ["Ineffective_outcome"])
X_v1 = model_df_v1[features_v1]
y_v1 = model_df_v1["Ineffective_outcome"]

X_train1, X_test1, y_train1, y_test1 = train_test_split(X_v1, y_v1, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
clf_v1 = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, class_weight="balanced")
clf_v1.fit(X_train1, y_train1)

auc_v1 = roc_auc_score(y_test1, clf_v1.predict_proba(X_test1)[:,1])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6,5))
ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_estimator(clf_v1, X_test1, y_test1, ax=ax)
plt.title(f"Outcome-Based Target | ROC-AUC: {auc_v1:.3f}")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

---

## Approach 1: Why It Fell Short

::: {.incremental}
- **ROC-AUC ≈ 0.56** — barely better than a coin flip
- A ball call is a **noisy proxy** for fatigue:
  - Intentional pitches off the zone
  - Catcher framing misses
  - Close takes unrelated to pitcher mechanics
- The label has too much noise for biomechanical deviations to overcome
- We need a **cleaner, more direct** definition of fatigue
:::

---

## Approach 2: Threshold-Based Target

**Insight:** instead of predicting an umpire's call, directly predict **velocity decline**

$$y = \mathbf{1}[\text{VeloDev} < -1 \text{ mph}]$$


`SpinDev` · `IVBDev` · `EffectiveVeloDev` · `HorzBreakDev` · `ExtensionDev` · `PitchCount`

::: {.callout-note}
The question becomes: **can other biomechanical signals predict when velocity tanks?**
:::

---

## Approach 2: Results

```{python}
data_all["Ineffective"] = (data_all["VeloDev"] < -1).astype(int)
features_v2 = ["SpinDev","IVBDev","EffectiveVeloDev","HorzBreakDev","ExtensionDev","PitchCount"]
model_df_v2 = data_all.dropna(subset=features_v2 + ["Ineffective"])
X_v2 = model_df_v2[features_v2]
y_v2 = model_df_v2["Ineffective"]

X_train2, X_test2, y_train2, y_test2 = train_test_split(X_v2, y_v2, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
clf_v2 = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, class_weight="balanced")
clf_v2.fit(X_train2, y_train2)

auc_v2 = roc_auc_score(y_test2, clf_v2.predict_proba(X_test2)[:,1])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6,5))
ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_estimator(clf_v2, X_test2, y_test2, ax=ax)
plt.title(f"Threshold-Based Target | ROC-AUC: {auc_v2:.3f}")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

**Accuracy: 90% · Recall (fatigue): 92% · ROC-AUC: 0.976**

---

## Approach 2: Coefficient Plot

```{python}
coef_df = pd.DataFrame({"Feature":features_v2,"Coefficient":clf_v2.coef_[0]}).sort_values("Coefficient")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9,5))
ax.barh(coef_df["Feature"], coef_df["Coefficient"])
ax.axvline(0, color="red")
ax.set_title("Logistic Regression Coefficients — Threshold Target")
ax.set_xlabel("Coefficient")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.incremental}
- **EffectiveVeloDev** strongly negative — perceived velocity drop predicts actual velocity loss
- **ExtensionDev** positive — possible overextension compensation mechanism when fatigued
- SpinDev, IVBDev, PitchCount add minimal independent signal
:::

---

## Comparing the Two Approaches

| | Outcome-Based | Threshold-Based |
|---|---|---|
| **Target** | Ball call | VeloDev < −1 mph |
| **ROC-AUC** | 0.56 | 0.976 |
| **Recall (fatigue)** | 59% | 92% |
| **Key issue** | Noisy label | Clean, direct signal |
